SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
SUM_CR="${SUM_CR:-0}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-}"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"cacheRead":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${SUM_CR}" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} cached=${SUM_CR} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE=""
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))' > "${NEXT_FILE}"
  jq -n \
    --rawfile next "${NEXT_FILE}" \
    --arg branch "${DATA_BRANCH}" \
    --arg message "leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]" \
    --arg sha "${SHA}" \
    '{branch: $branch, message: $message, content: ($next | @base64)} + (if $sha != "" then {sha: $sha} else {} end)' > "${BODY_FILE}"
  if gh api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}" --input "${BODY_FILE}"; then ok=1; break; fi
  echo "token publish attempt ${attempt} conflicted — refetching"
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done
if [ "${ok}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts (concurrent writes) — rows are decorative, next legs retry"
fi

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1154
- **Title**: fix(token_usage): use --input temp file for Contents API PUT to avoid E2BIG (#1152)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/gh-1152-tokens-put-e2big` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +357
- **Deletions**: -42
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:26:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:35:35Z

## PR Description

## Summary
Fixes the `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long` at Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 131,072 bytes) failure when publishing `data/fa-tokens.json` to `factory-data`.

## Root Cause
- On `IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, `data/fa-tokens.json` on `factory-data` reached **96,174 bytes** (525 legs across 197 keys) at commit `21a0fb08f7da33cc5de24f796da306d551e3418c` (`leg tokens — pr-1665 rework [skip ci]`, `2026-10-19T14:22:28Z`).
- `contentsPutCommand` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` (and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) constructed:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/contents/<dataPath> -f branch=... -f message=... -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
- At 96,174 bytes of raw JSON, base64 encoding (`4/3` + line wraps) produced **129,927 bytes** for the single CLI argument `content=<base64>`. The very next leg pushed `content=<base64>` past the Linux kernel `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit (**131,072 bytes / 128 KiB** per single argument in `execve`), causing `/bin/sh` / `gh` to fail with `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long`) on all 3 retries and silently give up (`::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts`).
- Because `data/fa-tokens.json` froze at `pr-1665`, `fetchTokensFromBranch` had no entries for `pr-1715+`, so `tmap['pr-' + pr.number]` missed on 100% of active cards in `data/fa-state.json`.

## Changes
1. **`js/factory/token_usage.js`**:
   - Added runtime-agnostic `base64EncodeUtf8(str)` and `buildContentsPutBody(o)` (`{ branch, message, content, sha? }`).
   - Added `--input <tempPath>` transport (`tempPutBodyPath`, `contentsPutInputCommand`, `tryPutViaInputFile`, `putTokenContents`) following the `checkRunStamp.js` pattern (`file_write` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input <tempFile>` + `file_delete` in `finally`), keeping the shell command string under 200 bytes regardless of payload size while preserving legacy `contentsPutCommand` fallback when `io.write` is not injected.
2. **`js/factory/token_usage_publish.js`**:
   - Wired `file_write` and `file_delete` into the `publishTokenUsage` IO adapter alongside `cli_execute_command` and `file_read`.
3. **`scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`**:
   - Replaced `-f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)"` with temp files (`jq -n --rawfile next ... '{branch, message, content: ($next | @base64)}'` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input "${BODY_FILE}"`).
4. **`js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js`**:
   - Added unit tests for `base64EncodeUtf8` (ASCII, padding, multi-byte UTF-8), `buildContentsPutBody`, `--input` temp-file lifecycle, and a >100 KB raw JSON (>131,072 bytes base64) regression test verifying the shell command stays <200 bytes.

Closes #1152

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1154._

> ℹ️ **4 resolved thread(s) excluded; 1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

🚨 **BLOCKING: new tests use Node `Buffer` — the canonical dmtools-java gate is red**

`AGENTS.md` ("GraalJS Constraints"): *"No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages."* The three new assertions call `Buffer.from(...)`:

```js
var expected = Buffer.from(utf8Sample, 'utf8').toString('base64');          // test_factoryTokenUsage.js:309
Buffer.from(withoutSha.content, 'base64').toString('utf8')                  // :323
Buffer.from(parsedBody.content, 'base64').toString('utf8')                  // :373
```

Verified on this PR's HEAD:

```
$ dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
  ❌ FAIL  —  5779 passed, 3 failed
  ❌ base64EncodeUtf8 encodes empty, ASCII, padding … 'Buffer' is not defined
  ❌ buildContentsPutBody produces branch, message, base64 content … 'Buffer' is not defined
  ❌ publishTokenUsage with write/del uses --input temp file … 'Buffer' is not defined
```

`quality.yml` treats this exact runner as the gate ("Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job)"), so the PR turns CI red. The node harness passes only because Node *has* `Buffer` — it is the wrong oracle for this repo.

Fix without `Buffer` (same coverage):
- Replace the round-trip checks with hardcoded expected literals computed once (e.g. `node -e "console.log(Buffer.from('<sample>','utf8').toString('base64'))"` pasted into the test, in the `'Zg=='` / `'Zm8='` / `'Zm9v'` style already used), and/or
- add a tiny pure-JS base64 **decoder** helper inside the test file to decode + `JSON.parse` the `content` field — same assertions, zero Node APIs.

Note the encoder itself is fine: the 120 KB regression test (the one new test that does **not** use `Buffer`) passes in the canonical runtime — only these assertions need reworking.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: silent fallback to the E2BIG-prone inline PUT**

`putTokenContents` falls back to the legacy inline argv builder whenever `io.write` is not wired:

```js
return tryExec(io && io.exec, contentsPutCommand(repo, path, putOpts));
```

`contentsPutCommand` is the exact transport gh-1152 fixes: at ≥96 KB of JSON the single `content=<base64>` argument crosses Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072 bytes) and **every** retry fails with `E2BIG`. On a runtime without the `file_write` global (the `envValue` doc in `token_usage_publish.js` itself notes the QuickJS runtime gives no guarantees), this silently reverts to the broken path: 3 doomed retries, then only the generic `::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts` — the very failure this PR closes, now harder to diagnose.

Suggestion: emit a one-time distinguishable warning when the fallback is taken, e.g.
`log('::warning::file_write unavailable — inline argv PUT fallback (E2BIG risk at ≥96 KB payloads)')` (io.log is already in scope), and/or carry the chosen transport in the result so operators can tell the two failure modes apart.

Related nit (same diagnosability theme, unchanged line below): any failure — including a `file_write` error — logs as `token publish attempt N conflicted — refetching`, conflating real 409 conflicts with write/transport errors.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: deterministic temp path — no random component**

`tempPutBodyPath` derives the path solely from `now` (ms) + attempt number. Two concurrent publishes landing in the same millisecond with the same attempt (e.g. matrix legs on a shared self-hosted runner) would target the same `/tmp/fa-tokens-put-<ms>-<attempt>.json`, and one run could overwrite/delete the file while the other's `gh api --input` is mid-flight — with a wrong body attributed to the other leg's key.

Notably, the sh side of this same PR uses `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX"` — random suffix, collision-free. It also follows the `checkRunStamp.js` precedent (`tempBodyPath`, same `Number(now)` scheme), so this is consistent with existing JS-side convention — hence a suggestion, not a blocker. A random suffix (where entropy is available) or at least a comment acknowledging the shared-ms trade-off would make the asymmetry with the sh transport explicit.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: arm the EXIT trap between the two `mktemp` calls**

The trap is armed only after both temp files exist:

```bash
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
```

If the second `mktemp` fails, `set -e` exits the script and `NEXT_FILE` leaks. Move the `trap` line between the two `mktemp` calls — `BODY_FILE` is then unset at arm time, and `rm -f ""` (quoted empty) tolerates it. Negligible on ephemeral GitHub runners; cheap to harden for self-hosted reuse.

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Fixed in e1b3c626: replaced all `Buffer.from(...)` calls in `test_factoryTokenUsage.js` with a pure-JS `base64DecodeUtf8` helper + hardcoded expected base64 literal, so `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` runs cleanly on GraalJS and QuickJS.

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Fixed in e1b3c626: `putTokenContents` now logs a one-time `::warning::file_write unavailable — inline argv PUT fallback (E2BIG risk at >=96 KB payloads)` when `io.write` is absent and the payload is >=96 KB, covered by unit test.

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Documented in e1b3c626 on `tempPutBodyPath` (matches the `checkRunStamp.js` `tempBodyPath` convention; each CI leg runs in its own container/step).

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Fixed in e1b3c626: `trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT` is now armed immediately after creating `NEXT_FILE` (with `BODY_FILE=""` initialized beforehand).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One blocking issue: the new tests use Node's `Buffer`, which the dmtools GraalJS runtime does not provide (banned by AGENTS.md), so the canonical gate `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` fails (5779 passed, **3 failed** — `'Buffer' is not defined`). The gh-1152 transport fix itself is sound — the 120 KB `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` regression test passes in the canonical runtime; only the Buffer-based assertions need reworking.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 **Blocking**: `Buffer.from(...)` at `js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js:309/323/373` → 3 failures in the canonical dmtools-java gate (details inline).
- ⚠️ `putTokenContents` silently falls back to the E2BIG-prone inline PUT when `file_write` is unavailable (`js/factory/token_usage.js:359`) — add a distinguishable warning (inline).
- ⚠️ *(outside diff)* `js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:1379` (`tokensPutAttempt`) still publishes `data/<asset>.json` through the legacy inline argv PUT — same unbounded growth (≤40 rows × N keys), same 128 KiB `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` wall this PR fixes for fa-tokens. Recommend a follow-up reusing `putTokenContents`.
- 💡 *(outside diff)* `js/factory/README.md:62-63` still says the entry wires only exec/read — now stale (write/del added); the retry log "conflicted — refetching" conflates file-write failures with 409 conflicts.

**Next Steps**:
1. Rework the three Buffer assertions (precomputed literals or a pure-JS decoder) until `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` is green.
2. Add the fallback warning in `putTokenContents`.
3. Optional: trap ordering in `publish-token-usage.sh`, random temp suffix, README wording, and a gh-1152 follow-up ticket for `aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter`.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# (step: Publish leg token usage (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)) — stage-1 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block + always() stay on the workflow step.
set -eu
if [ ! -s "${RUN_OUTPUT}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no run output captured — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT SUM_CR MODEL < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = cr = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # fa-tokens carries cacheRead per segment (gh-1241); the
        # board prices it (model-pricing cacheRead rates) and
        # renders an `input cached` column — sum it like in/out.
        cr += int(rec.get("cacheRead") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, cr, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
SUM_CR="${SUM_CR:-0}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-}"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"cacheRead":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${SUM_CR}" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} cached=${SUM_CR} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE=""
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))' > "${NEXT_FILE}"
  jq -n \
    --rawfile next "${NEXT_FILE}" \
    --arg branch "${DATA_BRANCH}" \
    --arg message "leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]" \
    --arg sha "${SHA}" \
    '{branch: $branch, message: $message, content: ($next | @base64)} + (if $sha != "" then {sha: $sha} else {} end)' > "${BODY_FILE}"
  if gh api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}" --input "${BODY_FILE}"; then ok=1; break; fi
  echo "token publish attempt ${attempt} conflicted — refetching"
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done
if [ "${ok}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts (concurrent writes) — rows are decorative, next legs retry"
fi

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1154
- **Title**: fix(token_usage): use --input temp file for Contents API PUT to avoid E2BIG (#1152)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/gh-1152-tokens-put-e2big` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +357
- **Deletions**: -42
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:26:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:35:35Z

## PR Description

## Summary
Fixes the `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long` at Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 131,072 bytes) failure when publishing `data/fa-tokens.json` to `factory-data`.

## Root Cause
- On `IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, `data/fa-tokens.json` on `factory-data` reached **96,174 bytes** (525 legs across 197 keys) at commit `21a0fb08f7da33cc5de24f796da306d551e3418c` (`leg tokens — pr-1665 rework [skip ci]`, `2026-10-19T14:22:28Z`).
- `contentsPutCommand` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` (and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) constructed:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/contents/<dataPath> -f branch=... -f message=... -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
- At 96,174 bytes of raw JSON, base64 encoding (`4/3` + line wraps) produced **129,927 bytes** for the single CLI argument `content=<base64>`. The very next leg pushed `content=<base64>` past the Linux kernel `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit (**131,072 bytes / 128 KiB** per single argument in `execve`), causing `/bin/sh` / `gh` to fail with `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long`) on all 3 retries and silently give up (`::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts`).
- Because `data/fa-tokens.json` froze at `pr-1665`, `fetchTokensFromBranch` had no entries for `pr-1715+`, so `tmap['pr-' + pr.number]` missed on 100% of active cards in `data/fa-state.json`.

## Changes
1. **`js/factory/token_usage.js`**:
   - Added runtime-agnostic `base64EncodeUtf8(str)` and `buildContentsPutBody(o)` (`{ branch, message, content, sha? }`).
   - Added `--input <tempPath>` transport (`tempPutBodyPath`, `contentsPutInputCommand`, `tryPutViaInputFile`, `putTokenContents`) following the `checkRunStamp.js` pattern (`file_write` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input <tempFile>` + `file_delete` in `finally`), keeping the shell command string under 200 bytes regardless of payload size while preserving legacy `contentsPutCommand` fallback when `io.write` is not injected.
2. **`js/factory/token_usage_publish.js`**:
   - Wired `file_write` and `file_delete` into the `publishTokenUsage` IO adapter alongside `cli_execute_command` and `file_read`.
3. **`scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`**:
   - Replaced `-f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)"` with temp files (`jq -n --rawfile next ... '{branch, message, content: ($next | @base64)}'` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input "${BODY_FILE}"`).
4. **`js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js`**:
   - Added unit tests for `base64EncodeUtf8` (ASCII, padding, multi-byte UTF-8), `buildContentsPutBody`, `--input` temp-file lifecycle, and a >100 KB raw JSON (>131,072 bytes base64) regression test verifying the shell command stays <200 bytes.

Closes #1152

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1154._

> ℹ️ **4 resolved thread(s) excluded; 1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

🚨 **BLOCKING: new tests use Node `Buffer` — the canonical dmtools-java gate is red**

`AGENTS.md` ("GraalJS Constraints"): *"No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages."* The three new assertions call `Buffer.from(...)`:

```js
var expected = Buffer.from(utf8Sample, 'utf8').toString('base64');          // test_factoryTokenUsage.js:309
Buffer.from(withoutSha.content, 'base64').toString('utf8')                  // :323
Buffer.from(parsedBody.content, 'base64').toString('utf8')                  // :373
```

Verified on this PR's HEAD:

```
$ dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
  ❌ FAIL  —  5779 passed, 3 failed
  ❌ base64EncodeUtf8 encodes empty, ASCII, padding … 'Buffer' is not defined
  ❌ buildContentsPutBody produces branch, message, base64 content … 'Buffer' is not defined
  ❌ publishTokenUsage with write/del uses --input temp file … 'Buffer' is not defined
```

`quality.yml` treats this exact runner as the gate ("Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job)"), so the PR turns CI red. The node harness passes only because Node *has* `Buffer` — it is the wrong oracle for this repo.

Fix without `Buffer` (same coverage):
- Replace the round-trip checks with hardcoded expected literals computed once (e.g. `node -e "console.log(Buffer.from('<sample>','utf8').toString('base64'))"` pasted into the test, in the `'Zg=='` / `'Zm8='` / `'Zm9v'` style already used), and/or
- add a tiny pure-JS base64 **decoder** helper inside the test file to decode + `JSON.parse` the `content` field — same assertions, zero Node APIs.

Note the encoder itself is fine: the 120 KB regression test (the one new test that does **not** use `Buffer`) passes in the canonical runtime — only these assertions need reworking.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: silent fallback to the E2BIG-prone inline PUT**

`putTokenContents` falls back to the legacy inline argv builder whenever `io.write` is not wired:

```js
return tryExec(io && io.exec, contentsPutCommand(repo, path, putOpts));
```

`contentsPutCommand` is the exact transport gh-1152 fixes: at ≥96 KB of JSON the single `content=<base64>` argument crosses Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072 bytes) and **every** retry fails with `E2BIG`. On a runtime without the `file_write` global (the `envValue` doc in `token_usage_publish.js` itself notes the QuickJS runtime gives no guarantees), this silently reverts to the broken path: 3 doomed retries, then only the generic `::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts` — the very failure this PR closes, now harder to diagnose.

Suggestion: emit a one-time distinguishable warning when the fallback is taken, e.g.
`log('::warning::file_write unavailable — inline argv PUT fallback (E2BIG risk at ≥96 KB payloads)')` (io.log is already in scope), and/or carry the chosen transport in the result so operators can tell the two failure modes apart.

Related nit (same diagnosability theme, unchanged line below): any failure — including a `file_write` error — logs as `token publish attempt N conflicted — refetching`, conflating real 409 conflicts with write/transport errors.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: deterministic temp path — no random component**

`tempPutBodyPath` derives the path solely from `now` (ms) + attempt number. Two concurrent publishes landing in the same millisecond with the same attempt (e.g. matrix legs on a shared self-hosted runner) would target the same `/tmp/fa-tokens-put-<ms>-<attempt>.json`, and one run could overwrite/delete the file while the other's `gh api --input` is mid-flight — with a wrong body attributed to the other leg's key.

Notably, the sh side of this same PR uses `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX"` — random suffix, collision-free. It also follows the `checkRunStamp.js` precedent (`tempBodyPath`, same `Number(now)` scheme), so this is consistent with existing JS-side convention — hence a suggestion, not a blocker. A random suffix (where entropy is available) or at least a comment acknowledging the shared-ms trade-off would make the asymmetry with the sh transport explicit.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: arm the EXIT trap between the two `mktemp` calls**

The trap is armed only after both temp files exist:

```bash
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
```

If the second `mktemp` fails, `set -e` exits the script and `NEXT_FILE` leaks. Move the `trap` line between the two `mktemp` calls — `BODY_FILE` is then unset at arm time, and `rm -f ""` (quoted empty) tolerates it. Negligible on ephemeral GitHub runners; cheap to harden for self-hosted reuse.

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Fixed in e1b3c626: replaced all `Buffer.from(...)` calls in `test_factoryTokenUsage.js` with a pure-JS `base64DecodeUtf8` helper + hardcoded expected base64 literal, so `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` runs cleanly on GraalJS and QuickJS.

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Fixed in e1b3c626: `putTokenContents` now logs a one-time `::warning::file_write unavailable — inline argv PUT fallback (E2BIG risk at >=96 KB payloads)` when `io.write` is absent and the payload is >=96 KB, covered by unit test.

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Documented in e1b3c626 on `tempPutBodyPath` (matches the `checkRunStamp.js` `tempBodyPath` convention; each CI leg runs in its own container/step).

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Fixed in e1b3c626: `trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT` is now armed immediately after creating `NEXT_FILE` (with `BODY_FILE=""` initialized beforehand).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One blocking issue: the new tests use Node's `Buffer`, which the dmtools GraalJS runtime does not provide (banned by AGENTS.md), so the canonical gate `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` fails (5779 passed, **3 failed** — `'Buffer' is not defined`). The gh-1152 transport fix itself is sound — the 120 KB `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` regression test passes in the canonical runtime; only the Buffer-based assertions need reworking.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 **Blocking**: `Buffer.from(...)` at `js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js:309/323/373` → 3 failures in the canonical dmtools-java gate (details inline).
- ⚠️ `putTokenContents` silently falls back to the E2BIG-prone inline PUT when `file_write` is unavailable (`js/factory/token_usage.js:359`) — add a distinguishable warning (inline).
- ⚠️ *(outside diff)* `js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:1379` (`tokensPutAttempt`) still publishes `data/<asset>.json` through the legacy inline argv PUT — same unbounded growth (≤40 rows × N keys), same 128 KiB `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` wall this PR fixes for fa-tokens. Recommend a follow-up reusing `putTokenContents`.
- 💡 *(outside diff)* `js/factory/README.md:62-63` still says the entry wires only exec/read — now stale (write/del added); the retry log "conflicted — refetching" conflates file-write failures with 409 conflicts.

**Next Steps**:
1. Rework the three Buffer assertions (precomputed literals or a pure-JS decoder) until `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` is green.
2. Add the fallback warning in `putTokenContents`.
3. Optional: trap ordering in `publish-token-usage.sh`, random temp suffix, README wording, and a gh-1152 follow-up ticket for `aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter`.

---

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# (step: Publish leg token usage (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)) — stage-1 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block + always() stay on the workflow step.
set -eu
if [ ! -s "${RUN_OUTPUT}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no run output captured — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT SUM_CR MODEL < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = cr = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # fa-tokens carries cacheRead per segment (gh-1241); the
        # board prices it (model-pricing cacheRead rates) and
        # renders an `input cached` column — sum it like in/out.
        cr += int(rec.get("cacheRead") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, cr, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
SUM_CR="${SUM_CR:-0}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-}"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"cacheRead":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${SUM_CR}" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} cached=${SUM_CR} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE=""
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))' > "${NEXT_FILE}"
  jq -n \
    --rawfile next "${NEXT_FILE}" \
    --arg branch "${DATA_BRANCH}" \
    --arg message "leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]" \
    --arg sha "${SHA}" \
    '{branch: $branch, message: $message, content: ($next | @base64)} + (if $sha != "" then {sha: $sha} else {} end)' > "${BODY_FILE}"
  if gh api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}" --input "${BODY_FILE}"; then ok=1; break; fi
  echo "token publish attempt ${attempt} conflicted — refetching"
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done
if [ "${ok}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts (concurrent writes) — rows are decorative, next legs retry"
fi

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1154
- **Title**: fix(token_usage): use --input temp file for Contents API PUT to avoid E2BIG (#1152)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/gh-1152-tokens-put-e2big` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +357
- **Deletions**: -42
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:26:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:35:35Z

## PR Description

## Summary
Fixes the `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long` at Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 131,072 bytes) failure when publishing `data/fa-tokens.json` to `factory-data`.

## Root Cause
- On `IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, `data/fa-tokens.json` on `factory-data` reached **96,174 bytes** (525 legs across 197 keys) at commit `21a0fb08f7da33cc5de24f796da306d551e3418c` (`leg tokens — pr-1665 rework [skip ci]`, `2026-10-19T14:22:28Z`).
- `contentsPutCommand` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` (and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) constructed:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/contents/<dataPath> -f branch=... -f message=... -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
- At 96,174 bytes of raw JSON, base64 encoding (`4/3` + line wraps) produced **129,927 bytes** for the single CLI argument `content=<base64>`. The very next leg pushed `content=<base64>` past the Linux kernel `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit (**131,072 bytes / 128 KiB** per single argument in `execve`), causing `/bin/sh` / `gh` to fail with `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long`) on all 3 retries and silently give up (`::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts`).
- Because `data/fa-tokens.json` froze at `pr-1665`, `fetchTokensFromBranch` had no entries for `pr-1715+`, so `tmap['pr-' + pr.number]` missed on 100% of active cards in `data/fa-state.json`.

## Changes
1. **`js/factory/token_usage.js`**:
   - Added runtime-agnostic `base64EncodeUtf8(str)` and `buildContentsPutBody(o)` (`{ branch, message, content, sha? }`).
   - Added `--input <tempPath>` transport (`tempPutBodyPath`, `contentsPutInputCommand`, `tryPutViaInputFile`, `putTokenContents`) following the `checkRunStamp.js` pattern (`file_write` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input <tempFile>` + `file_delete` in `finally`), keeping the shell command string under 200 bytes regardless of payload size while preserving legacy `contentsPutCommand` fallback when `io.write` is not injected.
2. **`js/factory/token_usage_publish.js`**:
   - Wired `file_write` and `file_delete` into the `publishTokenUsage` IO adapter alongside `cli_execute_command` and `file_read`.
3. **`scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`**:
   - Replaced `-f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)"` with temp files (`jq -n --rawfile next ... '{branch, message, content: ($next | @base64)}'` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input "${BODY_FILE}"`).
4. **`js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js`**:
   - Added unit tests for `base64EncodeUtf8` (ASCII, padding, multi-byte UTF-8), `buildContentsPutBody`, `--input` temp-file lifecycle, and a >100 KB raw JSON (>131,072 bytes base64) regression test verifying the shell command stays <200 bytes.

Closes #1152

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1154._

> ℹ️ **4 resolved thread(s) excluded; 1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

🚨 **BLOCKING: new tests use Node `Buffer` — the canonical dmtools-java gate is red**

`AGENTS.md` ("GraalJS Constraints"): *"No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages."* The three new assertions call `Buffer.from(...)`:

```js
var expected = Buffer.from(utf8Sample, 'utf8').toString('base64');          // test_factoryTokenUsage.js:309
Buffer.from(withoutSha.content, 'base64').toString('utf8')                  // :323
Buffer.from(parsedBody.content, 'base64').toString('utf8')                  // :373
```

Verified on this PR's HEAD:

```
$ dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
  ❌ FAIL  —  5779 passed, 3 failed
  ❌ base64EncodeUtf8 encodes empty, ASCII, padding … 'Buffer' is not defined
  ❌ buildContentsPutBody produces branch, message, base64 content … 'Buffer' is not defined
  ❌ publishTokenUsage with write/del uses --input temp file … 'Buffer' is not defined
```

`quality.yml` treats this exact runner as the gate ("Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job)"), so the PR turns CI red. The node harness passes only because Node *has* `Buffer` — it is the wrong oracle for this repo.

Fix without `Buffer` (same coverage):
- Replace the round-trip checks with hardcoded expected literals computed once (e.g. `node -e "console.log(Buffer.from('<sample>','utf8').toString('base64'))"` pasted into the test, in the `'Zg=='` / `'Zm8='` / `'Zm9v'` style already used), and/or
- add a tiny pure-JS base64 **decoder** helper inside the test file to decode + `JSON.parse` the `content` field — same assertions, zero Node APIs.

Note the encoder itself is fine: the 120 KB regression test (the one new test that does **not** use `Buffer`) passes in the canonical runtime — only these assertions need reworking.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: silent fallback to the E2BIG-prone inline PUT**

`putTokenContents` falls back to the legacy inline argv builder whenever `io.write` is not wired:

```js
return tryExec(io && io.exec, contentsPutCommand(repo, path, putOpts));
```

`contentsPutCommand` is the exact transport gh-1152 fixes: at ≥96 KB of JSON the single `content=<base64>` argument crosses Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072 bytes) and **every** retry fails with `E2BIG`. On a runtime without the `file_write` global (the `envValue` doc in `token_usage_publish.js` itself notes the QuickJS runtime gives no guarantees), this silently reverts to the broken path: 3 doomed retries, then only the generic `::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts` — the very failure this PR closes, now harder to diagnose.

Suggestion: emit a one-time distinguishable warning when the fallback is taken, e.g.
`log('::warning::file_write unavailable — inline argv PUT fallback (E2BIG risk at ≥96 KB payloads)')` (io.log is already in scope), and/or carry the chosen transport in the result so operators can tell the two failure modes apart.

Related nit (same diagnosability theme, unchanged line below): any failure — including a `file_write` error — logs as `token publish attempt N conflicted — refetching`, conflating real 409 conflicts with write/transport errors.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: deterministic temp path — no random component**

`tempPutBodyPath` derives the path solely from `now` (ms) + attempt number. Two concurrent publishes landing in the same millisecond with the same attempt (e.g. matrix legs on a shared self-hosted runner) would target the same `/tmp/fa-tokens-put-<ms>-<attempt>.json`, and one run could overwrite/delete the file while the other's `gh api --input` is mid-flight — with a wrong body attributed to the other leg's key.

Notably, the sh side of this same PR uses `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX"` — random suffix, collision-free. It also follows the `checkRunStamp.js` precedent (`tempBodyPath`, same `Number(now)` scheme), so this is consistent with existing JS-side convention — hence a suggestion, not a blocker. A random suffix (where entropy is available) or at least a comment acknowledging the shared-ms trade-off would make the asymmetry with the sh transport explicit.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: arm the EXIT trap between the two `mktemp` calls**

The trap is armed only after both temp files exist:

```bash
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
```

If the second `mktemp` fails, `set -e` exits the script and `NEXT_FILE` leaks. Move the `trap` line between the two `mktemp` calls — `BODY_FILE` is then unset at arm time, and `rm -f ""` (quoted empty) tolerates it. Negligible on ephemeral GitHub runners; cheap to harden for self-hosted reuse.

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Fixed in e1b3c626: replaced all `Buffer.from(...)` calls in `test_factoryTokenUsage.js` with a pure-JS `base64DecodeUtf8` helper + hardcoded expected base64 literal, so `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` runs cleanly on GraalJS and QuickJS.

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Fixed in e1b3c626: `putTokenContents` now logs a one-time `::warning::file_write unavailable — inline argv PUT fallback (E2BIG risk at >=96 KB payloads)` when `io.write` is absent and the payload is >=96 KB, covered by unit test.

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Documented in e1b3c626 on `tempPutBodyPath` (matches the `checkRunStamp.js` `tempBodyPath` convention; each CI leg runs in its own container/step).

---

**IstiN** (2026-10-21):

Fixed in e1b3c626: `trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT` is now armed immediately after creating `NEXT_FILE` (with `BODY_FILE=""` initialized beforehand).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-21):

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One blocking issue: the new tests use Node's `Buffer`, which the dmtools GraalJS runtime does not provide (banned by AGENTS.md), so the canonical gate `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` fails (5779 passed, **3 failed** — `'Buffer' is not defined`). The gh-1152 transport fix itself is sound — the 120 KB `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` regression test passes in the canonical runtime; only the Buffer-based assertions need reworking.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 **Blocking**: `Buffer.from(...)` at `js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js:309/323/373` → 3 failures in the canonical dmtools-java gate (details inline).
- ⚠️ `putTokenContents` silently falls back to the E2BIG-prone inline PUT when `file_write` is unavailable (`js/factory/token_usage.js:359`) — add a distinguishable warning (inline).
- ⚠️ *(outside diff)* `js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:1379` (`tokensPutAttempt`) still publishes `data/<asset>.json` through the legacy inline argv PUT — same unbounded growth (≤40 rows × N keys), same 128 KiB `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` wall this PR fixes for fa-tokens. Recommend a follow-up reusing `putTokenContents`.
- 💡 *(outside diff)* `js/factory/README.md:62-63` still says the entry wires only exec/read — now stale (write/del added); the retry log "conflicted — refetching" conflates file-write failures with 409 conflicts.

**Next Steps**:
1. Rework the three Buffer assertions (precomputed literals or a pure-JS decoder) until `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` is green.
2. Add the fallback warning in `putTokenContents`.
3. Optional: trap ordering in `publish-token-usage.sh`, random temp suffix, README wording, and a gh-1152 follow-up ticket for `aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter`.

---

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# (step: Publish leg token usage (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)) — stage-1 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block + always() stay on the workflow step.
set -eu
if [ ! -s "${RUN_OUTPUT}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no run output captured — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT SUM_CR MODEL < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = cr = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # fa-tokens carries cacheRead per segment (gh-1241); the
        # board prices it (model-pricing cacheRead rates) and
        # renders an `input cached` column — sum it like in/out.
        cr += int(rec.get("cacheRead") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, cr, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
SUM_CR="${SUM_CR:-0}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-}"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"cacheRead":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${SUM_CR}" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} cached=${SUM_CR} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE=""
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))' > "${NEXT_FILE}"
  jq -n \
    --rawfile next "${NEXT_FILE}" \
    --arg branch "${DATA_BRANCH}" \
    --arg message "leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]" \
    --arg sha "${SHA}" \
    '{branch: $branch, message: $message, content: ($next | @base64)} + (if $sha != "" then {sha: $sha} else {} end)' > "${BODY_FILE}"
  if gh api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}" --input "${BODY_FILE}"; then ok=1; break; fi
  echo "token publish attempt ${attempt} conflicted — refetching"
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done
if [ "${ok}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts (concurrent writes) — rows are decorative, next legs retry"
fi

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1154
- **Title**: fix(token_usage): use --input temp file for Contents API PUT to avoid E2BIG (#1152)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/gh-1152-tokens-put-e2big` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +357
- **Deletions**: -42
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:26:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:35:35Z

## PR Description

## Summary
Fixes the `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long` at Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 131,072 bytes) failure when publishing `data/fa-tokens.json` to `factory-data`.

## Root Cause
- On `IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, `data/fa-tokens.json` on `factory-data` reached **96,174 bytes** (525 legs across 197 keys) at commit `21a0fb08f7da33cc5de24f796da306d551e3418c` (`leg tokens — pr-1665 rework [skip ci]`, `2026-10-19T14:22:28Z`).
- `contentsPutCommand` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` (and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) constructed:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/contents/<dataPath> -f branch=... -f message=... -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
- At 96,174 bytes of raw JSON, base64 encoding (`4/3` + line wraps) produced **129,927 bytes** for the single CLI argument `content=<base64>`. The very next leg pushed `content=<base64>` past the Linux kernel `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit (**131,072 bytes / 128 KiB** per single argument in `execve`), causing `/bin/sh` / `gh` to fail with `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long`) on all 3 retries and silently give up (`::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts`).
- Because `data/fa-tokens.json` froze at `pr-1665`, `fetchTokensFromBranch` had no entries for `pr-1715+`, so `tmap['pr-' + pr.number]` missed on 100% of active cards in `data/fa-state.json`.

## Changes
1. **`js/factory/token_usage.js`**:
   - Added runtime-agnostic `base64EncodeUtf8(str)` and `buildContentsPutBody(o)` (`{ branch, message, content, sha? }`).
   - Added `--input <tempPath>` transport (`tempPutBodyPath`, `contentsPutInputCommand`, `tryPutViaInputFile`, `putTokenContents`) following the `checkRunStamp.js` pattern (`file_write` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input <tempFile>` + `file_delete` in `finally`), keeping the shell command string under 200 bytes regardless of payload size while preserving legacy `contentsPutCommand` fallback when `io.write` is not injected.
2. **`js/factory/token_usage_publish.js`**:
   - Wired `file_write` and `file_delete` into the `publishTokenUsage` IO adapter alongside `cli_execute_command` and `file_read`.
3. **`scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`**:
   - Replaced `-f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)"` with temp files (`jq -n --rawfile next ... '{branch, message, content: ($next | @base64)}'` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input "${BODY_FILE}"`).
4. **`js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js`**:
   - Added unit tests for `base64EncodeUtf8` (ASCII, padding, multi-byte UTF-8), `buildContentsPutBody`, `--input` temp-file lifecycle, and a >100 KB raw JSON (>131,072 bytes base64) regression test verifying the shell command stays <200 bytes.

Closes #1152
